name: Neck tension / platysma flex

lead: Platysma flexing means deliberately tightening the thin muscle across the front of the neck so the area under the jaw looks more defined, usually for a photo.
It is discussed as a posing technique rather than a lasting change. No published studies have examined it.

paras: The platysma sits just under the skin of the neck; contracting it tightens and wrinkles the overlying skin and can pull the lower lip and mouth corners downward [1].
No specific harms have been documented for the practice. Clinical sources note that prominent platysmal bands can be aggravated by some activities such as weightlifting [1]. No trials exist.

lead: Neck tension or platysma flexing is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which a person deliberately contracts the platysma, the thin superficial muscle of the neck, to make the jaw-neck transition and lower jawline look more defined, mostly for photographs or mirror checks.

The platysma is a broad, thin sheet that overlies the sternocleidomastoid. When it contracts it wrinkles the neck skin slightly and can pull down the lower lip and mouth corners [1]. Its visible bands become more noticeable with age and can be aggravated by weightlifting and some facelift procedures [1].
No published clinical studies have been found that test platysma flexing or neck exercises for jawline appearance.

paras: The platysma is supplied by the cervical branch of the facial nerve. Its anterior fibres can depress the lower jaw and pull down the lower lip and corners of the mouth, a smaller role than that of other facial depressor muscles [1].

Visible platysmal bands (sometimes called platysma dyskinesia or "turkey neck") tend to become more prominent with age [1]. Options described in clinical references include conservative management, botulinum toxin injection, platysmaplasty (open or closed) and neck liposuction [1]. These are separate from voluntary flexing as practised online.

lore.intro: Looksmaxxing communities discuss platysma flexing as a posing technique; no forum sources were reviewed for this entry.

claims.claim: Flexing the platysma makes the jawline and neck look sharper.
